utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Please be seated. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Good morning to the technical booth, the interpreters. Good morning registry staff, the counsel for the Prosecution and for the Defence. We will be resuming our case. I think that Ms. Susan Somers has something to say. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Yesterday I had promised the Chamber and counsel to report on the status of the use of the model of Keraterm in the Keraterm trial. I have spoken with the Prosecution representative there, and the model will not be used. Although the outside is satisfactory in terms of fair depiction of Keraterm in 1992, because it has a removable top, the inside when looked at, it has been considered -- it is not accurate, does not accurately depict the 1992 Keraterm, so we have elected not to -- the Prosecution has elected not to use the model. I have conveyed this a little while ago to Mr. Stojanovic and have indicated that some of the photographs which were provided by the Prosecution to the Defence and which are, in fact, being used in the Keraterm trial are better depictions, and I think probably will not confuse any person, any trier of fact or witness looking at them. The decision, of course, rests with Mr. Stojanovic, but we feel that there would be some objection, certainly to using the internal parts, regrettably, but I wanted to let the Chamber know the status.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stojanovic, do you wish to make a brief comment? We don't wish to waste too much time discussing the model, but please say whatever you have to say, but briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, after consultation with my co-counsel, we will use photographs. As we see that that would be a problem as there are several photographs, the Prosecution has offered to assist us and provide us some more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think that we can now call the witness. Mr. Usher, will you bring in the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness DD/2. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to continue your testimony. I remind you that you're still testifying under oath, and you will continue to answer questions that Mr. Saxon is going to put to you. Mr. Saxon, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just as a point of clarification, it's my understanding that I have 25 more minutes in which to complete this cross-examination, but I know I have been wrong before in terms of my mathematics, so I simply want to check that that is also the Trial Chamber's understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think your arithmetic is right, so please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May we please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let us go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness DD/2, while you were detained in the Keraterm camp, how were you treated by the other Muslim prisoners there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not well at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were quarrels, there was pushing around. Nobody was enjoying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What would you quarrel with the other Muslim prisoners about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What about? About food.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you present when a man wanted to slit your brother's throat with a knife, but Zoran Zigic protected him? Were you present on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What did Zoran Zigic do to protect your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said to my brother, "Come over here. Not a hair may be touched on your head."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What, if anything, did Zoran Zigic say to the man with the knife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told him to shove off, to get out, to leave the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did that man with the knife leave the compound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was Zoran Zigic liked by the other Muslim detainees at the Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How would you describe - and this is my last question - the reputation that Mr. Zigic had with the other Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He behaved correctly towards the other Muslim detainees. I know that he didn't beat anyone, except for this Car, once in the behind, that he kicked. I don't know he hit anyone else, and he didn't, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The Court's indulgence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Saxon. Mr. Deretic, I know you have some additional questions, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/2, you said yesterday that you went to Travnik on the 17th of September, 1994, from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You also said yesterday that upon reaching Travnik you were arrested.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After you arrived in Travnik, how much time went by until your arrest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Less than half an hour. Thirty minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Who arrested you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The police, the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Whose military police was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of the Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: At the time when you went to Travnik, was fierce fighting still going on in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: In those days, was there a very strict border between the territory controlled by the Serbs and the territory controlled by the Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were real borders between territories.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: In which part of the territory of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina was Travnik situated in those days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Near Turbek.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Under whose control was Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under the control of the Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After your arrest, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was that a civilian or a military prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A military prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know why you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Nobody told me anything. They just took me in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After your arrest, were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Who beat you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was beaten by soldiers and civilians, people from Kozarac, Sivci.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Who were these Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was their surname, Sivac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Six.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Were they wearing civilian clothes or in uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some were in uniform, some in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Whose uniform was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The uniform of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, were you beaten just once or several times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Non-stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: In addition to this beating, were you mistreated in any other way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you describe how you were mistreated in addition to beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was constantly called out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: The room you were put in after your arrest, what were the conditions like there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dreadful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you describe the room that you were put in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there were three wooden beds made of wooden boards, there was concrete on the floor, and military blankets.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was anyone else with you in that room as a detainee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you remember the name or names of those persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only my brother was with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was that your older or your younger brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My older brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: While you're talking, I can see that your teeth are missing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They knocked them out while I was there. I was covered in bruises. I was all black and blue. I couldn't drink water even. My brother also had all his teeth knocked out. He hasn't got one left, and he had all of them before.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you lose your teeth there in the room in which you were detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you remember what they used to beat you with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All kinds of things: their boots and truncheons and planks, whatever they could get hold of. They were under the effect of drugs, they were drunk.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't understand. Who was drugged and drunk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, those Sivac men, and the soldiers were drunk too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, allow me to repeat the question once again for the witness to answer, because I don't think the answer has been registered in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did the guards protect you when you were beaten up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They gave these soldiers and civilians the key to come in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Were you given food regularly while you were imprisoned in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only once, and that was in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What did you receive for dinner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, a soup of some kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was that enough as a meal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: During the time you were beaten, did anybody interrogate you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you notice on that occasion that the minutes were taken of your interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How many times did they interrogate you in that way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you mean when you were in prison in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Witness DD/2, when were you transferred to the prison in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 14th of October, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Were you transferred to the Zenica prison directly from that prison in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How long did you spend in the prison in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, I apologise for interrupting, but could you tell us, please, how much time you're going to need for your redirect, because what you are doing now seems to me to be more in the line of an examination-in-chief rather than a redirect.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is my intention to question the witness for five more minutes, but all the questions relate precisely to the statement presented and introduced by the Prosecution during the witness's cross-examination, so I beg the Court's indulgence for another five minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: While you were in Zenica, were you beaten there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Who beat you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The police did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: During the time you spent in Travnik and Zenica, did you give a statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just gave my statement with respect to when they imprisoned me in Travnik, and I have a decision, my own decision on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you give the contents of that statement that the Prosecution has presented to you? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this could possibly be in Travnik, but I don't remember this statement, and eight or nine years have gone by since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: While you were in Travnik and Zenica, during that period of time did you happen to go to Banja Luka ever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: On the statement that has been shown to you it says that it was compiled in the Security Service Centre of Banja Luka on the 11th of, on the 11th of October, 1994. Where were you then on that date? Where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Were you detained for the first time at that time before you were transferred to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that you were transferred from Travnik to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I was transferred to Zenica on the 14th of October, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you sign any kind of statement while you were in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The signature is mine, but it was all under duress.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Are you talking about the statement presented to you by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember having given this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You said you gave a statement. When you gave that statement, before you signed it, was it read back to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Never. I never read it myself, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Deretic. Judge Fouad Riad has the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Witness DD/2, good morning. Can you see me and hear me in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I'll just have a few questions to understand more what you said, and I'll start by the very end. You were just mentioning that you had to give a statement; you apparently gave a statement in Travnik. Do you remember if they forced you to make any false confessions and told you what to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Do you remember what it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was forced, under duress, because we were beaten. We were all beaten up and bloody, all black and blue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, but you don't know the content of what they wanted you to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And you signed without knowing anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I don't know. I don't remember. The signature is mine, but it was all under duress. I don't remember what. I didn't read it, nor did they read it to me, ever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, the fact is that you were -- the fact that you have been mistreated, you mentioned also you were mistreated in Kozarac by the civilians and also by the Bosniak soldiers, I suppose, if I understood rightly. What did they hold against you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in Kozarac, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: All right. Was it Zenica? I'm sorry, I don't know the place exactly. Wherever it was, it was -- it was by civilians, but Muslim civilians, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Travnik, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: In Travnik. What did they hold against you? You're one of them, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I remained until 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Remained where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Was that enough to, to hurt you in that manner, to be mistreated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: What did they want you to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because we didn't leave in 1992 to go and fight. I didn't want to go to war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Were there other people like you who were treated this way, many others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And that was also the reason you were put in gaol and treated almost like an enemy, badly and without any respect of human rights, as you said? All that because you do not go to war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Speaking of the other interrogation which was in Keraterm, so there was no torture in it, no beating like the one you had, like the one you had I think in Travnik? You had not at all -- were not at all beaten in Keraterm in the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, just once. I was beaten just once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: No. I see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Muslims beat me in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I'm speaking now of Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "The Muslims beat me more in Travnik," was what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good. But in Keraterm --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only once. I said they hit me only once, and that was in the WC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But you were not beaten during the interrogation. I noted that down. But did you see others being beaten in the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did you hear them, any sound of torture, of something, some brutality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, when you mentioned that you -- you mentioned, I think, that you saw Mr. Zigic three days after your arrival to Keraterm camp. Is that -- did I understand correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Then you said also in the cross-examination that I believe that you saw him only once.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And you said that he was very kind. He would never beat anyone. Now, seeing him only once, was that enough for you to judge that he was kind and would not beat anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It was enough? And this only time, he gave you food and cigarettes, as you said, or he gave you several times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He gave me that once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Only that once? So it only happened once? Everything happened once?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Fouad Riad. Madam Judge Wald has the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Witness, you talked in your testimony about the detainees Car and Emsud Bahonjic had been captured carrying guns of various kinds, and that seems to be a reason why they were specially singled out for attack in the camp. My question to you is you said you were there when Car arrived and was beaten and made to run in the circles with the gun on him. Did you actually see Car arriving still having the gun on his, or the same with Emsud Bahonjic? Were they still carrying the guns when they arrived, or did you just hear about the fact that they had been carrying guns when they were captured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This man Car came with a machine-gun, and Emsud Bahonjic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I'm sorry, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And Emsud Bahonjic came with a rifle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So you saw them getting off of a police van still carrying a Singapore rifle and a machine-gun? They were allowed to be carrying those guns as they got out of the police van and arrived at the camp? That's what you saw; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. You also told us that on the night of the "massacre," you saw things out of the openings in the door, or the netting or whatever, the apertures in the door in Room 1; right? You said you could see out of the openings in the door in Room 1, where you were, as to some of the things that were happening during the shooting, during the shootings directed toward Room 3. Isn't that what you told us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was just outside, in the morning. I saw those dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Let me clarify that. I'm glad you helped me out. I thought you had told me - but tell me if I'm wrong - I thought you had told us that you could actually see out the door in number 1 to what was happening during the period of the shootings. Is that wrong, and now you are just saying that when you came out the next morning you saw the bodies, but you didn't actually see anything happening that night? Which is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just saw in the morning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- the dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: That's very helpful. So you didn't see anything that night that was actually happening. Okay. As far as the bodies go, you told us about the AutoTransport truck being there in front of number 3. My question is: Were all the bodies, the dead bodies and the wounded, able to be transported in one trip by that truck? Did the truck -- was the truck able to get all the wounded and dead bodies or did it have to make more than one trip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So could you approximate for us or give us just a notion of how many bodies fitted into that truck for that one trip, just a general notion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't tell you when I don't know how many bodies there were, but they could all fit in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Well, maybe you could tell me whether it was dozens or hundreds. You must have that kind of an estimate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 150.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. And one question, one last question following up from Judge Riad. You clarified in your answer to him that you had just seen Mr. Zigic once, and I think then that you only sold the cigarettes for him once. Is that right? Was that your answer to Judge Riad: Just that one time you saw him and you got your cigarettes from him, just that one time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. And you also told us at other times in the testimony that you described what he wore and how he looked, and you said that he behaved nicely, but you also said that sometimes he would be shouting or using a loud voice. So in the one time that you saw him, he behaved nicely, or he was shouting, or he both behaved nicely and was shouting, and that was the one time that you got the cigarettes and that you saw him kicking Car once; all that happened in the one time, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just saw him hit Car once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Yes, but you also -- everything else you said about him in your testimony, about how nicely he behaved, whether he shouted, how he looked, the fact that you sold cigarettes -- he gave you cigarettes to sell for him, that all happened in one episode, is that right, on one day, on the arrival of Car's day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Madam Judge Wald. Witness, to continue along those lines, how many times did you -- for how long did you see Zigic when you saw him that one time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him just the once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but for how long? Two minutes, two hours, two days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A whole day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: A whole day. [Interpretation] Do you remember the date, perhaps, more or less?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember the date or the day when you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember the date when you arrived in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that you said that you were interrogated four or five days after your arrival, so do you know the date when you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when I arrived I was completely beside myself, completely lost.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to go back to the incident with Car. You said at one particular point that they started to beat him immediately, or words to that effect. I think that when you say "they started," that you mean the soldiers. Is that right? Am I understanding you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And Zoran Zigic, was he present or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember how many times this incident -- how long the incident with Car lasted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't really remember so well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. You also stated that among the soldiers beating Car, you did not see Zoran Zigic among those soldiers. Now, was Zigic present or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You also said that Emsud Bahonjic arrived on the 8th of June, 1992, and that he had come from Kozarac, brought in by the police; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why do you happen to remember that date so exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because the months were close next to each other. July follows June, August follows July, and August was when I left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you felt more lost at the beginning, when you -- did you feel more lost when you came to the camp, at the beginning, or towards the end of your stay there? Because you said that you didn't know the date because you felt lost, you felt beside yourself, and I can understand that, but how come you recalled that particular date so well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I asked the other detainees, the other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You asked the other prisoners what day it was; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When Emsud Bahonjic arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And why did you ask what date it was? Did you have a specific reason why you did that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I just asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Very well. I think that Mr. Deretic asked you the following question, whether Emsud Bahonjic was dead or was killed. You said, "I don't remember." Now, in your memory, was there some sort of knowledge that you forgot, and if so, what was that information? Did you forget --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember about Emsud Bahonjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have this question, and that's where the problem lies. If somebody asked me whether I knew whether he was -- Bahonjic was killed or just died, I would say, "I don't know." But you said, "I don't remember," which means that you might have known, you might have had some information about that, but that now you are unable to recall that information to remember it. So there's a difference there, and is there a difference when you say, "I don't remember" or "I don't know"? Is there a difference in your mind when you say those two, "I don't remember," or when you say "I don't know"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. With respect to Drago Tokmadzic, you said that he succumbed on the 20th of June. Now, I am asking you now: How did you know -- how did you learn -- how did you come to learn that particular date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because one of the soldiers mentioned it, that the soldier said that Drago Tokmadzic had succumbed to beating that particular June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know the soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you were washing the truck, a soldier arrived, you said, and your brother -- actually, you said that your brother called a guard called Sisic [phoen]. Do you know that guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not Sisic [phoen]. Kicic [phoen]. The guard's name was Kicic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. But it wasn't Zigic, at any rate. It wasn't Zigic; it was Kicic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say Zigic. You said Sisic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Very well. You also said that Emsud Bahonjic was beaten inside Room 1. Do you know who beat him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. Well, the soldiers and the police. There were a lot of us there in that particular room. We were all one on top of another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To wind up one more question, you said in connection with this statement shown to you by the Prosecutor, at a certain point you said, "This is my signature, but under pressure, under duress." Do you confirm that you said that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You also said, "I don't remember giving that statement." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say you don't remember. You don't remember having said, "I don't remember giving such a statement," or you don't remember having made that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember giving a statement, giving such a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's fine. That is sufficient for me. How can you say that you do not remember having made this statement, but you also say that you signed it under duress? How can both happen at the same time, not remembering a statement and saying that you signed it under duress?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was giving the statement, I was beaten up. I was totally lost, and I'm saying I don't remember now. So all this was under duress because we were beaten when we were making those statements, because that is the only way they could force us to make such a statement, by beating us up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. We have no more questions for you, Witness DD/2. Thank you very much for coming, and we wish you a safe journey home. Don't move for the moment because we need to pull down the blinds, and I'm going to ask the usher to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I think it's time, a good moment for a break before we begin with a new witness, so we're going to have a half-hour break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Before we have the witness brought in, merely to clarify something, you are not going to ask for the admission of that statement, Mr. Saxon, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we are not. Pursuant to the rules of this Trial Chamber, we are not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes. [Interpretation] Very well. In any way, it has been marked for identification, so if you were going to tender it, you knew what the ruling of the Chamber is, and that is really a prior statement in the sense of our ruling from the very beginning, so we maintain our decision. There's no need to make a decision because you are not requesting its admission, so this was simply to make things quite clear. Thank you for your cooperation. Now, Mr. Deretic or Mr. Stojanovic, who will be the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence for Mr. Zigic calls our fourth witness, Mr. Ivica Sikic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, bring in the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Ivica Sikic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please read the solemn declaration given to you by the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Thank you very much for coming. You will first be answering questions put to you by Mr. Deretic. Mr. Deretic, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sikic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to tell us your full name?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Ivica Sikic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Will you give us your mother's name and your father's name?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: My mother's name was Jela, and my father's name Mato.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 2nd of October, 1954, in Zuna.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What municipality does Zuna belong to?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: In those days, they belonged to the municipality of Ljubija, and today Zuna belongs to the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I am a Croat, and my religion is Catholicism.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Where are you residing now?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I'm living in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I do, two, a son and a daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Since when have you known him?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I have known him since 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Is your house in the same district as Zigic's house? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is in the same neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Zigic's parents?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I do know Zoran Zigic's parents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What is their name?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Zigic's mother's name is Savka and his father's name is Nikola.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Before the war, during the war, and today, have you socialised?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we socialise, as we are close neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Before the war broke out in the former Bosnia-Herzegovina, do you know where Zoran Zigic resided?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Before the war, you're asking me? I didn't quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Zoran Zigic was in Prijedor before the war?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Before the war started, Zoran was in Pula, and then he came to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Prior to the outbreak of war, were you employed?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I was employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Where were you employed?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I was working in Impro-Prijedor, a factory for the processing of meat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After the war broke out, were you mobilised to the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After being mobilised, did you see Zoran Zigic again?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I would see Zoran Zigic only when I came home on leave, when we went home for a change of clothing, and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me: As a member of the Croatian people, as a Croat, why did you respond to the call-up to join the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Why? It's a rather big question, but I'll try to answer it. One, I accepted the authorities that were in Prijedor at the time; number 2, my wife is Serb; and finally, I wanted to remain in the area where I was born and where my property is. I had a nice job and I wanted to keep that job.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sikic, do you know when the Serbs took over power in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. On the 1st of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: I didn't quite hear the date. Would you be kind enough to repeat the date?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: In the morning of the 1st of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After the takeover of power, did anything change for you? Did you continue working?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I continued working.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After the takeover of power in Prijedor, did you see Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Would you see him when he came home?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him when he came home. Of course, I didn't see him at work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: On those occasions, was he wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What kind of uniform was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: A blue police uniform, camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did he continue to wear that blue camouflage uniform later on?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Afterwards he didn't, after 15 or 20 days, something like that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What kind of uniform did Zigic wear later on?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: He wore a military camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did he wear a cap of any kind?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. He wore a beret.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the colour of the beret?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: The beret? It was red.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, in that time period, did a part of -- did Zoran have an injury on any part of his body?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. He had an injury of the left hand; actually, his fingers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know when Prijedor was attacked?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Prijedor? Prijedor was attacked a month after the takeover of power, so it was the 30th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You said 30 days after the takeover of power. A moment ago in answer to my question as to when power was taken over in Prijedor, you said it was the 1st of April, 1992, so that's a month earlier. So what would be the right date?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Between the 30th of March and the 1st of April was the takeover.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: During the takeover itself, do you know -- or rather, let me rephrase that. When Prijedor was attacked, do you know whether there was fighting in town?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, but I was with my unit at the time, there was fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to whether there were any dead on that day?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were dead in Prijedor that day, both among the policemen and the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After Prijedor was attacked, are you aware of the formation of investigation centres?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware that such centres were formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Could you list them for us?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Keraterm, Omarska, Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: As a soldier in those days, did you know who was detained in those investigation centres?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Persons were taken to those centres who would not accept the authorities, people who refused to surrender their weapons and people who took part in the attack on Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: In what part of town is your family home?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: My family home is in Cirkin Polje, which is on the slopes of Mount Kozara, at the foot of Mount Kozara.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sikic, could you tell us what the ethnic composition was of your neighbourhood? Were they all of the same ethnicity or of several ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: They belonged to several ethnic groups. It was multi-ethnic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge after the formation of these investigation centres whether any of your neighbours were taken to one of those three investigation centres?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: From our neighbourhood or district, no one was taken to the investigation centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know why?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Because nobody took part in the attack on Prijedor. They accepted the authorities, and that is why there was no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Zoran Zigic was a member of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know as of when and which unit he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: He first belonged to a police unit, and then he transferred to regular units, that is, the 43rd unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to a military formation?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, a military formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What does the 43rd mean?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: It is the name of a unit, the number of the unit, or the military post, as it was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sikic, could you tell us what you think about Zoran Zigic as a neighbour before the war and during the war?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Zigic Zoran as a neighbour, he was an extremely good neighbour. We socialised before the war, during the war. As neighbours, he would help us. We would go fishing together, hunting before the war. We would go on picnics. We helped one another whenever it was necessary. He was an extremely good neighbour. The only thing was when he had a little too much to drink.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What was he like when he had too much to drink?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: He had to be in the centre of attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What do you mean by saying that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Well, then everyone had to look at him, and he expected to be treated as a Rambo. He liked to joke, to tell stories, to sing, to play.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was he querulous in that condition?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, after the war operations had started and when you were already in uniform and when Zoran was in uniform, did you -- were you able to sense any change in his behaviour towards you because you were a member of another ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, none whatsoever. We remained as close as ever. In fact, I think he paid even greater attention to my family when I was not there. He took even greater care of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, were there any Muslims in your neighbourhood, people of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were, but mostly from mixed -- they were mostly mixed marriages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you happen to notice whether Zoran behaved towards those people in a different way afterwards than he did before the war?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sikic, do you have any knowledge about an event when, in Keraterm, several people were killed in the course of one night?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know when that event took place?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: That event took place between the 24th and 25th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember where you were on that particular night?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: That night, that night we were in the yard, in Zoran Zigic's yard or, rather, his father's yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And why were you there?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: We went there because we had agreed to have a barbecue that evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Before that particular event, was it customary for you to have barbecues in the Zigic house, and did they go to your home for barbecues?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was no problem. They would either come to us or we would go to them because we lived close by.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was that customary, usual?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was always usual. Before the war, during the war as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you remember when you arrived at the Zigic yard that evening?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: At the Zigic yard? About 20 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did anybody come with you on the occasion?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, my wife came with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember in addition to you and your wife whether there were any other people present in the Zigic yard that evening?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were his parents, his wife, two daughters, and afterwards some more people, young men, turned up.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When you came to the Zigic yard, did you see Zoran in the yard? Was he there?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was there when we arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How many people were there on the occasion?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Well, they would come in and gather there. At about 10.00 p.m., there might have been about 10 of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When you yourself came, you said that Zoran was there.

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What state was he in?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Well, he had had quite a lot to drink, but not so much that he wasn't able to stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: The people, the guests that gathered, can you remember whether you all came at once or you came one by one and then all gathered there? What was the time frame?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: We didn't come all at once. We would come in one by one. We would gather there. We gathered there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did some young men turn up who played some music?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. There were two young men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may we go into private session for a few moments now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let us move into private session, please, for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ivica Sikic, you said a moment ago that the guests gathered over a period of two hours, they kept coming in over that period of time. Now, during that period of time, do you happen to know whether Zoran was in the yard throughout that time?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: On two occasions Zoran went to get some bread. That was the first time. And as we had run out of drinks, he went to get more drinks. And I would go back to my own home to bring some things like some more meat and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long he was away when he went to get those things?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Well, not long. Just 10 to 15 minutes at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After all the guests had gathered, did Zoran leave the yard at all?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Until 10.00 p.m., Zoran did not leave the yard. I'm sorry. After 10.00 p.m., Zoran did not leave the yard, as far as I remember. He did not leave the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sikic, who left the Zigic yard first, you and your wife or Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Zoran left first, before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Where did Zoran go?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Zoran was dead drunk and he went into the house. That is to say, I helped him get into the house and lie down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us at what time Zoran went in to go to sleep?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Zoran went in at about midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You said that you helped him go in to lie down.

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you go into the house with him, actually?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I went into the house, into the kitchen, and helped him lie down on the couch.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Zoran had any weapons on him then?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He had a pistol, and as he was very drunk, he put the pistol under the pillow.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: After Zoran lay down to sleep, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: We continued sitting around in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Now, before midnight that same evening, did you happen to hear any shooting in town? Was there any shooting before midnight?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Well, that was standard practice. You would hear sporadic gunfire, shots going off, that kind of thing. That was usual, customary.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did anything unusual happen after midnight?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: After midnight something unusual did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Well, there was some strong shooting and then there was very heavy shooting. There was a burst of gunfire, a long burst of gunfire with intermittent pauses, but all this went on for quite some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did the guests that you were sitting around with in the yard make any comments about that shooting in town?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Somebody said, "Well, someone's going to say again Zigic has gone mad again."

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you know at the time where the shooting was happening and who was doing the shooting?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Where was Zoran at that time?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Zoran was in the kitchen, lying on the couch. He was dead drunk at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I know because I went to the WC several times, and as it's a glass door, I would see him lying there, so that's how I know he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: In view of his state of intoxication when you led him into the house, did Zoran -- was Zoran able to leave the house? Was he capable of leaving the house?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't capable, because he was so drunk. He was going about on all fours, practically.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: The Zigic yard, can you describe it for us, for the Trial Chamber? In relation to the town, where is the Zigic yard?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Well, the yard to the house of Zigic's parents is on an incline. Prijedor is down in a valley, on a flat, whereas our houses are on a slope, at an altitude of about 80, 90 metres above sea level, compared to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Where was the Keraterm Investigation Centre located?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: The investigation centre of Keraterm was located to the left of the Prijedor-Banja Luka road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You said a moment ago, if I'm not wrong, that you would go hunting often with Zoran.

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that was before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: So I assume you'll be able to answer my following question. Can you tell us, please, taking it as the crow flies, how far Keraterm is away from the Zigic yard?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: You say as the crow flies? Well, as the crow flies, the Zigic yard and Keraterm is about 800 to 1.000 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When did you leave the Zigic yard?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: We left the Zigic yard between 3.00 and 4.00 a.m., perhaps 3.30, but between 3.00 and 4.00 a.m. I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did your wife go with you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, my wife left too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When you left for home, did you hear any shooting?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, you could hear shooting, but it was sporadic, not as frequent.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You said that your house was about 50 metres away from the Zigic yard; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When you arrived home, did you comment, make any comments to your wife about the shooting? Did you and your wife comment about that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't comment about the shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Upon arriving home, did you know where the shooting was coming from?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know where the shooting was coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When did you learn something about that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I learnt about it the next day when I went in to town and met my colleagues there. We sat down in a cafe and that was what they were talking about. They --

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And what did you learn?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: My colleagues told me who had gone by there that a large number of people were killed in Keraterm, had been killed in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sikic, at the beginning of your testimony you stated that you do know something about Zoran's injury, wounding.

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know that later on he was -- Zoran was injured again, wounded again?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Can you remember when and where he was wounded?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: On the 19th of August in Gomjenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sikic, do you happen to remember what year that was?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: It was the month of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When he was injured, was your son in the company of Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How old was your son at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Do you know in what part of his body Zoran Zigic was injured on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: He was injured around his chin.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Where were you on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I was with my unit at the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How did you learn about this event and when did you learn about it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I learnt about it in the evening because my -- do you want me to explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I wasn't there that day, and in the evening when my commander came for consultations in Prijedor, I learnt about it. He took me into a room and he explained to me what had happened nice and slowly. And he gave me permission to take a car in the morning to go to Prijedor and to settle those problems because the vehicle had been confiscated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What vehicle was that about?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: It was my own private car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: On that day, did Zoran Zigic use your personal car?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He used it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Was your son with him in the car on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, my son was with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: On that day, was your son kidnapped by Zoran Zigic, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: How, then, did it happen that Zigic was driving your car?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Well, that was quite usual. If I wasn't there and he needed the car, he would drive the car, and I would be -- I would drive his if I needed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: In Cirkin Polje, which is where your house is located -- or rather, let me rephrase that. Who came to Cirkin Polje before, your family or Zigic's family?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, Zigic's family was there first.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: When did you yourself come to Cirkin Polje?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Since 1980, have you known Zoran Zigic since 1980?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: What kind of hair did Zoran Zigic have at the time?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: He had black hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did his hair colour ever change to the present day? Did he ever change his hair colour?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see him dyeing his hair? It's modern today to do that, so did you ever see him dye his hair?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see since 1980 Zoran Zigic wearing earrings?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, he never had an earring, wore an earring.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: You also said that you saw him when you came home on leave from your unit, that you would see him then, and that Zoran was wearing a uniform at the time.

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you see him armed then?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: At the time, everybody carried a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see Zigic, Zoran, use black gloves with the fingers cut off?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: And the last question, my last question for you, Mr. Sikic, how could you describe Zigic, Zoran, as a person from that time and generally speaking? What kind of a man is Zoran Zigic? How could you describe him for us?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I could describe Zigic, Zoran, in the following way: Before the war he was a very good friend, a good comrade. When he was sober, he was all milk and honey, but when he would have some drink, then he would like to be the focus of his attention, and he would be prepared to give you blood from his own veins. I can only speak for myself. During the war he was always proper, always good as a neighbour, as a friend, as a co-fighter. I don't know what else I could say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Sikic.

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Deretic. Witness, you are now going to answer questions put to you by the Prosecutor. I think it is going to be Ms. Susan Somers who will be cross-examining you. Your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, do I understand that no Defence counsel wish to ask questions? I can proceed, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I should have asked. I see negative signs from the other Defence counsel. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'd like to pick up on a point you just made, Mr. Sikic, actually, two points. One is, what is your wife's first name, please?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: My wife's name is Zoka Sikic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And did your wife appear in this very courtroom earlier this week also on behalf of Mr. Zigic? Is that the same person?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You mentioned that you first learned about Mr. Zigic's August injury from your commander. Did your son not tell you about that injury?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid there must be a misunderstanding regarding this point. The attorney asked me when Zigic was wounded for the second time. I said in Gomjenica, and my commander told me the details about what happened on that 19th of August, that my son was there in the car.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And did your son himself tell you about those injuries?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I came home he told me the whole story, of course, as he would to a parent.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your son told you the whole story. Now, did your son tell you what preceded the injuries, where he and Mr. Zigic were just before the injuries happened?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me where they went. He just told me that they were shot at, at the checkpoint, that Zoran was hit in the chin, and that he fell over him, and that he thought that Zoran was dead, and he started crying. And I wasn't interested in any further details.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did it concern you that your son found himself in a rather dangerous situation, in other words, in a car where the driver was being shot at -- actually, in your car where the driver whom you entrusted with that car was being shot at? Did that concern you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: It didn't concern me that my son was with Zoran in the car, but of course I was concerned by the shooting. Like any parent, I was uncomfortable.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did your son tell you that Mr. Zigic had taken your car and gone to the home of an individual, a Muslim individual named Edin Ganic, and had demanded money from Mr. Ganic? Did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me anything about that. Maybe he was hiding it from me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did he tell you that at Mr. Ganic's house on the 19th of August, 1992, there was a Serb woman named Mara, either Kusanjic or Kusanjic, who was visiting the Ganics? Did he mention that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't mention that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did he mention that Mr. Zigic had stabbed this Serb woman Mara who was visiting Ganics? Did he mention that she was stabbed by Mr. Zigic?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No. No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How often have you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Deretic, yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in answer to a question by my learned friend whether the son had told his father anything about visiting the Ganics, the witness literally said that his son told him nothing, so I don't see the point of the three follow -- the questions that followed linked to the visit to the Ganic house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, your response?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The witness said that the son told his father, as a son would, the whole story, and I'm inquiring into the parts which go into the whole story, and apparently not all of the parts were told to make the whole story. I think that I can test the witness's knowledge of his version of what was told by trying to understand his understanding of our facts in our possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Put your questions, Ms. Susan Somers. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. On that particular question I'm satisfied with the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you, what is your young son's name, please, the son who was with Mr. Zigic at the time, his name?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Zeljko.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did any police officers come up to you afterward and ask about Zeljko's being in the presence of Mr. Zigic at that incident?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Policemen? Only when I came home, I went to the military police and took back my car. I was given the keys, and afterwards, I went back to my unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you ask Zigic yourself about the incident at the checkpoint? Did it concern you enough that your car was being fired at, at a checkpoint erected by the Serbs in whose army you were serving?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask Zigic, because I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Where were you assigned to fight when you were mobilised into the army of the Serbs or into the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: When I went to the Army of Republika Srpska, we were in the area of Mount Kozara.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When did you actually get mobilised? Date, please, month and year.

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: The 15th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you take part in any of the JNA actions against your own people in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did take part.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Where and when, please?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: The 16th of September, 1990 -- or 1991, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In other words, you, as a member of the army, were fighting against Croats in Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: It is correct, but in those days it was the Yugoslav People's Army. There was Yugoslavia, and it was normal for me to respond to mobilisation and to join the unit I was assigned to and I belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And to fight against your own people, was that normal?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I responded to the call-up to my unit. I didn't know against whom I was going to fight.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And you were taken to Croatia how?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: I was taken there together with my unit, which is quite normal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Have you been to Croatia since, since it became an independent state?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have been, twice. No, I'm sorry. Three times last year.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Going back to the evening of the 24th of July, please clarify: At whose house was this barbecue taking place? Was it Zigic's house, the accused, or the house of his parents?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: Zigic's parents and Zigic lived together in the same house. The same house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: From your description of your relationship, it appears that you were very close to Zoran Zigic. Did you have a relationship that would be described as almost family?

utterances.speaker: IVICA SIKIC
utterances.text: No, we were not family, but we were close, because we have a rule: First look at your neighbour and then at the sun [Realtime transcript read in error "son"]. So a neighbour is somebody very important.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
